newsitem.title: USA: Woman soldier says she feared sergeant's rank.
newsitem.headline: Woman soldier says she feared sergeant's rank.

text.p: An Army private told a military jury Thursday that she did not resist having sex with her drill sergeant because she feared the power of his rank.

The 20-year-old private had already been placed on a 90-day disciplinary measure when she said drill sergeant Delmar Simpson initiated oral sex and intercourse with her in his office and in her room on two occassions in 1996.

She said Simpson knew staying in the Army was important to her because she had told him so, and he helped her out of the disciplinary matter. When he made the advances, the private from Tennessee neither resisted or reported the incident to authorities, fearing Simpson could have her discharged.
"He was an E-7 and my drill sergeant. I was an E-1, nothing. I had been in trouble before. Even if I did (reported) who would believe me?" the private said.

Simpson, 32, has been charged with 19 counts of rape and 39 other charges including indecent exposure, battery, and maltreatment involving 13 women. He pleaded innocent to those charges but pleaded guilty earlier to 11 counts of improper sexual intercourse with trainees and five of propositioning.

The Simpson case is the first trial among 12 soldiers charged in the military's biggest sex scandal since the Navy's 1991 Tailhook affair and he was charged with the most crimes. Four other cases were resolved through plea agreements or administrative proceedings.

Much of the testimony of Simpson's alleged victims has been similar. According to witnesses who have testified in the trial which began last Friday, many of the alleged sexual encounters took place in Simpson's office after he called them there individually.
As testimony continued in the case Thursday morning, the female private from Tennessee and another from Clarksburg, Pa., each described their alleged assaults.
The Tennessee woman said the second assault was interrupted when another drill sergeant knocked on the door and warned Simpson that a high-ranking soldier was approaching.

Under cross-examination, the witness acknowledged telling investigators Simpson didn't force her to do anything, and that she neither physically nor verbally resisted. She said she did not want Simpson to know that she did not want to have sex with him. But, she said, "I didn't feel like I could say no, sir."

The Pennsylvania soldier said Simpson first exposed himself to her when he called her to his office. He allegedly raped her on two other occasions there. The second rape took place on the floor of a small bathroom where Simpson had ordered her to go and wait for him.
She told two friends about the incident but did not know what superior she could trust and who would believe her, she said. Seeing Simpson every day, "made me sick to my stomach," she said.
The soldier's testimony was to continue in the afternoon.
